review_notes: I read the whole file and checked its simp interface against related Mathlib files. The only `@[simp]` lemmas here are `zero_lt_two`, `zero_lt_three` and `zero_lt_four`. They are stated for general ordered `AddMonoidWithOne` types with `NeZero 1`. They are not subsumed by `Nat.ofNat_pos` (in `Mathlib/Data/Nat/Cast/Order/Ring.lean`), which needs `Semiring`, `IsOrderedRing` and `Nontrivial`, or by `Nat.ofNat_pos'`, which is `simp low`. They also cause no rewrite loop, because each one closes a `0 < n` goal and rewrites nothing. The non-simp lemmas (`zero_le_two`, `zero_le_three`, `zero_le_four`, `one_le_two`, `one_le_two'`, `one_lt_two`, `lt_add_one`, `lt_one_add`) are covered or reasonable. `Nat.ofNat_nonneg'` is `simp low`, `Nat.one_le_ofNat` and `Nat.one_lt_ofNat` are `simp`, and `lt_add_iff_pos_right` together with `zero_lt_one` should handle `a < a + 1`. The primed primes (`zero_lt_two'` and so on) are deliberately not simp, because they would duplicate the unprimed rules. The only possible gap is that `one_lt_two` is not simp in the strictly-monotone, non-`CharZero` setting. I did not find a use or a failing case showing that this matters. I did not run Lean, so I cannot confirm how the simp sets interact in practice.
